ops.title: rapid-mlx 0.10.9 is metal's production LLM engine since 2026-07-13 (commit 89ed6b5, replaced omlx). Measured: int8 KV 17.9 tok/s / int4 25.9 / omlx was 8.6; prefix cache + MTP are no-ops on the hybrid GatedDeltaNet model; ~101 s load (HEALTH_TIMEOUT 150);
ops.body:
**Engine.** metal:8000 runs **rapid-mlx 0.10.9** (PyPI `rapid-mlx`, launchd `org.nixos.rapid-mlx`) since 2026-07-13, commit 89ed6b5 — replacing omlx after the qmlx/Rapid-MLX evaluation ([[qmlx-gate0-spike-2026-07]]). Serve line (darwin/metal.nix): model `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-MLX-4bit` (models.nix now holds the real slashed HF id; omlx's `--` mangling is dead), `--host $TSIP --port 8000 --max-num-seqs 1 --kv-cache-dtype int8 --pflash off` + blog sampling defaults; env `HF_HUB_CACHE` (hfhub share) + `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. Lazy venv at `~/.venvs/rapid-mlx` built from brew `/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14` (system python3 is 3.9.6 — too old); upgrade lever = bump pin in metal.nix, `rm -rf ~/.venvs/rapid-mlx`, `yclaw bounce metal rapid-mlx`.

**Measured (this exact VM + model, 2026-07-12/13):**
- Decode: omlx 8.6 tok/s → rapid-mlx **25.9 (int4 KV default)** / **17.9 (int8, the deployed dtype — picked for tool-call/KV fidelity)**. int4 is a one-line lever if throughput ever outranks precision.
- Prefix cache is a **no-op on this hybrid GatedDeltaNet model in every engine's disk/radix cache** (0 entries, re-prefills every turn, ~7.5 s per ~2k prompt); omlx's in-mem block cache was the only thing that ever warmed it (~4 s) — that reuse was traded for 3× decode. MTP/spec-decode is architecturally disabled on hybrids (even the MTP-weights variant); only the Metal kernel-JIT cache survives restarts (~14 s first-large-prefill penalty paid once ever).
- Load→LISTEN ≈ **101 s** (cold 20 GB virtiofs re-read). `yclaw/restart.py` HEALTH_TIMEOUT raised 30→150 for this. Model is always-resident (no idle unload, unlike omlx).
- `--pflash off` is deliberate: pflash lossily compresses prompts (2994→2304 tok) — unacceptable for tool calling.
- Tool calls verified end-to-end from hermes vantage: auto-selected `tool_call_parser=qwen3_coder_xml`, `reasoning_parser=qwen3`; structured tool_calls with valid JSON args; `message.content` non-empty on plain chat (the omlx#903 empty-content bug does NOT reproduce on rapid-mlx).
- Alias `qwen3.6-35b-ud` → our exact unsloth quant; served offline zero-download.

**Model pick (2026-07-13, user-ratified): keep Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.** A 15-agent selection workflow (ground → 3 web sweeps → 5 dossiers + adversarial verify) found the incumbent at the Pareto frontier: everything smarter in ≤30 GB is dense (~1 tok/s in this VM — Qwen3.6-27B, Granite 4.1 30B) or busts the bound (Qwen3-Next-80B ~40 GB); everything faster is dumber (Gemma 4 26B-A4B, gpt-oss-20b, Nemotron Nano). Runner-up if warm-TTFT ever matters more than IQ: **GLM-4.7-Flash** (16.85 GB, MIT, full-attention MLA → prefix cache would actually work; but GPQA 75 vs 86, needs a glm47 tool parser). Rejected: OptiQ mixed-quant sibling (MTP head unusable on hybrids; confirmed tool-call failures + "endless loops with Hermes" reports). Context: the local model is the LAST fallback (hit only when gpt-5.5 AND gemini both fail), and vision never routes to it (hardcoded openai) — so per-request intelligence outweighs TTFT.

**Rollback + follow-ups:** omlx brew formula + jundot/omlx tap are still installed on the live VM (deliberate rollback window) — post-soak cleanup = `brew uninstall omlx && brew untap jundot/omlx` on metal + delete the dated 2026-07-12 cleanup block in metal.nix. `git revert 89ed6b5` + redeploy restores omlx in minutes (weights never moved). Reboot survival: plist has RunAtLoad/KeepAlive + wait4path trampoline; nightly-bounce + reboot gates unverified as of 2026-07-13. build-images CI was chronically red (runner lacked KVM) until the 2026-07-13 systemd-repart migration ([[repart-image-migration-facts]]) — green since.
